cards.name: Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2)
cards.buy_if: you want hands-free photos, calls, music and 'what am I looking at?' in frames you'd wear anyway.
cards.skip_if: your week includes gyms, courts, clinics or cinemas — you'll be asked to take them off.
cards.owners: Owners call them addictive fun. Complaints: privacy defaults, and features that arrive months late.

cards.name: Meta Ray-Ban Display
cards.chip: Colour screen in the lens · Neural Band
cards.buy_if: you want directions, captions and messages floating in your lens today.
cards.skip_if: your prescription is outside ±4, or you want a screen for movies (that's XR glasses).
cards.owners: Owners are wowed by the display and the wristband. Complaints: 6-hour battery, and 69 g on the nose.

cards.name: Rokid Glasses
cards.chip: Screen in both eyes · 49 g · ChatGPT or Gemini
cards.buy_if: you want a screen in both lenses and your choice of AI, for $200 less than Meta's.
cards.skip_if: you want a colour display or the Meta app ecosystem.
cards.owners: Owners praise the weight and the AI switch. Complaints: green-only text, and a weak low-light camera.
cards.video_title: Techmong: taking Korea's college entrance exam wearing Rokid AI glasses

cards.name: Even Realities G2
cards.chip: No camera · discreet HUD · days of battery
cards.buy_if: you want translation, navigation and notes in a lens nobody can tell is smart.
cards.skip_if: you want photos or music — there's no camera and no speakers.
cards.owners: Owners praise the discreet design and the after-sales service. Complaint: green monochrome text only.

cards.name: Xreal One Pro
cards.buy_if: you fly a lot, game on a Steam Deck, or work in a tiny space.
cards.skip_if: you have a Lightning iPhone (no video out) or a Switch 2 without the Xreal Hub.
cards.owners: Owners love the cinema-on-a-plane effect. Complaints: 87 g on the nose, and compatibility puzzles.

cards.name: Viture Luma Pro
cards.buy_if: you want the sharpest, most comfortable picture for the money.
cards.skip_if: you want Xreal's built-in screen anchoring and software tricks.
cards.owners: Owners praise the sharpness and the electrochromic dimming. Complaint: fewer software features.

cards.name: Oakley Meta Vanguard
cards.buy_if: you run, ride or ski and want a centred POV camera and loud speakers.
cards.skip_if: you want to wear them to dinner — they look like sports gear.
cards.owners: Owners praise the battery and the camera angle. Complaints: sound leaks, and the sporty look.

cards.name: Rokid AI Glasses Style
cards.buy_if: you want camera-and-AI glasses without a Meta account, for $100 less.
cards.skip_if: styling matters to you — reviewers call them plain.
cards.owners: Owners like the price and the AI choice. Complaints: the looks, and a proprietary charger.

cards.name: Amazon Echo Frames (3rd Gen)
cards.buy_if: you want Alexa and audio in normal, prescription-ready frames.
cards.skip_if: you want a camera or an AI that can see.
cards.owners: Owners like the discreet audio. Complaints: battery life, and sound leaking to neighbours.

cards.name: Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 1)
cards.buy_if: you want the Meta experience at the lowest price and can live with a 4-hour battery.
cards.skip_if: you'd hate charging twice a day.
cards.owners: Owners say it's the best deal in smart glasses. The complaint is always the battery.
